title: fix(service-package): a restart serves the stored installedAt/updatedAt, not the boot time
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DH9e4qEZ6HPSFPqXCYcdFui)_

Fixes #33535

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:重启后 `sys_packages` 的启动回填不再把包的 `installedAt` / `updatedAt` 写成开机时间,而是取库里存的 `created_at` / `updated_at`。
- **为什么改**:管理员每次重启后看到的“安装时间”都变成重启时间,和库里的真实安装时间、以及 PATCH 已经保留 `installedAt` 的行为相矛盾。
- **风险与回滚**:低。只改 `service-package` 的回填路径,线上形状不变;新安装仍取当前时间。回滚 = revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/services/service-package/src/index.ts`(回填循环里的 `carryStoredLifecycleStamps` 调用与函数本体);`package-table.ts` 的 `packageStampToIso`;新测试 `installed-at-after-restart.test.ts`。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-package exec vitest run src/installed-at-after-restart.test.ts`,预期 3/3 通过(两次重启后 `installedAt` 仍是首次安装时刻)。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## Probe (before any edit)

Reproduced on `origin/main` 4bba8b8f02 with a real stack: ObjectQL + better-sqlite3 on a file + `PackageServicePlugin` + the metadata protocol, the restart being a second kernel boot on the same database file (the rig `latest-row-after-restart.test.ts` already uses). Install at 10:00:00Z, restart at 11:00:00Z: the registry record (which `GET /api/v1/packages/:id` projects field-for-field through `INSTALLED_PACKAGE_RESPONSE_FIELDS`) answered

```text
- "installedAt": "2026-11-14T10:00:00.000Z",  "updatedAt": "2026-11-14T10:00:00.000Z"   (expected)
+ "installedAt": "2026-11-14T11:00:00.000Z",  "updatedAt": "2026-11-14T11:00:00.000Z"   (received)
Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)
```

Mechanism confirmed as the card suspected: the hydrate calls `registry.installPackage(...)`, and `SchemaRegistry.installPackage` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) sets `installedAt: now, updatedAt: now` on every call.

## What changes

- The `sys_packages` boot hydration (`PackageServicePlugin.start`) carries the stored row's `created_at` onto the installed record as `installedAt`, and its `updated_at` as `updatedAt` (`carryStoredLifecycleStamps`). The registry keeps and hands out that record object (`collection.set(id, pkg); return pkg`), so the carry sets it in place, the same in-place discipline the protocol's `restorePackageRow` already relies on.
- `packageStampToIso` (`package-table.ts`) is the inverse of `packageRowStamp` / `packageWriteStamp`: it reads `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS[.mmm]` (UTC) back as an ISO instant, and answers `undefined` for anything else, so a row without a readable stamp keeps the registry's stamp exactly as today (no legacy-data migration).
- A fresh install, in any process, still stamps the moment it runs.

Design choice, recorded on the order's axes (correctness of what an admin reads first, then smallest change, then effort): the stamp lives in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, outside this card's file surface. Giving `installPackage` a stamps argument would be the more explicit seam but widens a shared engine API for one caller; carrying the stored times at the hydration seam, which is the only caller that rehydrates rows, fixes what the admin reads with a change confined to `service-package`.

Precision: `created_at` is stored to the whole second (`packageRowStamp`), so `installedAt` comes back truncated to the second after a restart; `updated_at` keeps milliseconds. `installedAt` is the installed version's first write (an upgrade's row), which matches what the live registry stamps at an upgrade. An overwrite re-install of the same version keeps its row's `created_at`, so after a restart it reads the version's first install, not the overwrite.

Other lifecycle stamps on the same path: `statusChangedAt` is not re-stamped for an enabled package (the registry carries it only when an existing record had one). For a package the boot seeds as disabled, the registry stamps `statusChangedAt: now`; `sys_packages` and the package-state store hold no such stamp, so there is nothing stored to carry and it is left as is (noted below). No `enabledAt` exists.

## Tests

- New `src/installed-at-after-restart.test.ts` (3 cases, real stack): stamps survive two restarts; an upgrade restarts as the upgrade (`installedAt` the version's install to the second, `updatedAt` its last write to the millisecond); a package installed after the restart still stamps its own install time.
- `src/package-table.test.ts`: `packageStampToIso` reads both stored forms back and refuses everything else.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-package test`: Test Files 13 passed (13), Tests 144 passed (144). `typecheck` exit 0 (`--listFiles` includes the new test).

Ablation (one-time, not kept): with the fix committed, `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` replaced the `carryStoredLifecycleStamps(installed, rec);` call (anchor 1 to 0, blob 49251c2f0516 to 675966d07632) and ran the new test: 2 failed, 1 passed (the two restart cases red, the fresh-install case green, as expected). Restored: blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty. The test imports `./index.js` from source, so no `dist/` rebuild was involved.

## Acceptance notes

- A package the boot seeds as disabled reads `statusChangedAt` as the boot time after a restart; no stored stamp exists to carry (registry seed in `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, store in `packages/runtime/src/package-state-host-store.ts`). Not measured over HTTP; noted, not filed.
- Enable/disable bump the registry's `updatedAt` but do not write `sys_packages`, so after a restart `updatedAt` reads the last manifest write rather than the last enable/disable. Noted, not filed.
